div.div: رَشَأٌ A young gazelle, (S, Msb, K,) that has become active, or in motion, (S, Msb,) or that has become strong, (K,) and has walked (S, Msb, K) with its mother: (K:) pl. أَرْشَآءٌ. (Msb, K.) [In the following saying, I find it written as though with medd; app. for the sake of assimilation to النِّسَآء:] عِنْدِى جَارِيَةٌ مِنَ النِّسَآءِ أَشْبَهُ شَىْء ٍ بِالرَّشَآءِ, meaning [I have with me a young woman most like to] the [young] gazelle: so in the A. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
